items: Mysterious Name
A function, variable or type whose name does not reveal what it does or holds; rename it, or clarify the design.
Duplicated Code
The same logic shape in multiple hunks/files; extract the shared shape where warranted.
Feature Envy
A method reaches into another object more than its own; move it onto the relevant data.
Data Clumps
The same fields/params travel together; use a suitable type when warranted.
Primitive Obsession
A primitive stands in for a domain concept; introduce a small type only when deserved.
Repeated Switches
Repeated dispatch cascades on the same type; share a map or use appropriate polymorphism.
Shotgun Surgery
A logical change scatters edits; gather related change into one module.
Divergent Change
A module changes for unrelated reasons; split responsibilities when real.
Speculative Generality
Abstraction/parameters/hooks for needs not in the spec; remove them.
Message Chains
Long navigation chains expose another object’s internals; hide the walk behind its owner.
Middle Man
A class/function mostly delegates; remove unnecessary delegation.
Refused Bequest
An implementer ignores most inherited behavior; prefer composition.

## What to build

Display Ready, Review, Blocked, and All in a distinct ticket queue mode or view. Keep these queues separate from initiative navigation.

Separate canonical ticket status, recorded workflow activity, and the next available action. A Review action means ready for review, not that a review currently runs.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Users can select Ready, Review, Blocked, and All without losing initiative navigation state.
2. Queue headings and active controls identify the selected queue. Initiative rows do not mix into the filtered ticket list.
3. Queue rows separate type, ID, title, ticket status, and next action. Blocking information remains subordinate but readable.
4. The interface displays active workflow activity only when recorded data supports that activity. Readiness alone does not imply active execution.
5. Opening a queue ticket reaches the correct canonical ticket and initiative or Ungrouped context. Return navigation restores queue selection and scroll position.
6. Existing queue membership and workflow safety rules remain authoritative. Display changes do not weaken action restrictions.
7. Empty queues display accurate recovery controls. The All shortcut matches its actual input behavior.
8. No selection means no empty action menu. Available actions display their target and disabled reasons.
9. Uppercase R refreshes. Lowercase r retains the existing Review action. Workspace shortcuts remain unchanged.
10. Live updates preserve the selected ticket by identity. If the ticket leaves the queue, the interface explains the change and selects a valid row.
11. A refresh failure retains readable content and blocks unsafe transitions. Loading and empty states remain distinct.
12. Structured fields remain readable at small terminal sizes and without colour. Existing action, copy, and Files behavior remains unchanged.

## Out of scope

Do not add search, new queue semantics, a new tracker backend, or new workflow transitions.

## Specification

The parent specification defines the complete product intent. This ticket implements only the approved slice.


## Testing decisions

Use the complete modal as the main automated test boundary. Send input through its public interface. Assert visible behavior and canonical targets.

Use the existing modal, explorer, and live-update test patterns. Use temporary stores for record and watcher behavior. Avoid assertions about private arrays or incidental text formatting.

Run the actual Pi modal for terminal acceptance. Inspect 40 by 12, 80 by 24, and 120 by 40 terminals. Inspect colour and monochrome presentation.

Keep existing action, copy, workspace shortcut, and workflow safety behavior intact. Preserve terminal-control sanitization and Unicode display widths.

## Completion evidence

Record the focused behavior checks and terminal observations. Include evidence for the changed screens and relevant failure states.

## Comments

The user approved this slice and its direct blockers during ticket decomposition.

## Pi project navigation

`/shared-context` opens the current project tracker with initiatives, then Ungrouped.
Ungrouped is a synthetic collection and stays visible with zero items. It has no initiative planning actions.
Initiative rows show the recorded phase and Items count separately from the title. Missing phases show unavailable; actions never supply a phase.
Press Enter to open an initiative summary and its children. Press Enter on a child to open its existing detail view.
Initiative and item overviews show a short summary and a Full description control. Press d, focus the control with Tab and press Enter or Space, or click the control to read the complete recorded body. Research, planning, and other item types keep their own overview and action controls.
The description reader replaces the content view. Its heading and Return control stay visible. Use Up/Down, PgUp/PgDn, or the visible page controls to scroll wrapped text. The > marker identifies reader or Return focus without colour.
Esc or Return restores the originating screen, selected child or event, and pane scroll position. Ancestor breadcrumbs leave the reader directly. Each project and workspace retains its own reader position. Files remains independent and keeps its existing insertion behavior.
Live body changes clamp the reader position to readable content. Empty descriptions say that no description is recorded. A failed refresh identifies the description as unreadable and retains the last readable body. Removal explains the change and returns to an available parent.
Child rows separate type, stable ID, title, and recorded state. Supporting references and workflow warnings appear below the primary fields.
Initiative child lists include research, executable tickets, planning records, and other supported canonical records. Items counts include every member. Ungrouped includes every record without initiative membership; dependency edges do not create membership.
Research and planning details show the recorded state, metadata, and body without ticket events, review counts, or worktree state. Research and planning use the existing To tickets and Grill commands when registered. Other non-executable types offer Ask Matt only. Missing commands explain why an action is disabled. Fresh-chat confirmation and unsent commands remain unchanged.
Live type changes replace ticket-only details and actions. Live membership changes retain the selected canonical record when it remains in the collection. Tracker/Files switches and ancestor navigation preserve selection.
Titles wrap. Narrow terminals wrap phase and Items on separate lines below the title. Use PgUp/PgDn to read long rows without changing selection. Resizing or row reflow brings the selected record back into view; unchanged layouts retain deliberate paging.
The > marker identifies a focused selection. The ◇ marker identifies an inactive selection; both retain the selection background.
Use Tab and Shift+Tab to focus ancestors, panes, and workspace controls. Press Enter or Space on an ancestor, or click it, to return directly.
Esc returns one level and restores the parent selection and scroll position. In compact terminals, returning from Events with Esc or the ticket ancestor shows the overview at its saved reading position. Live updates retain canonical selection; removal explains the new selection. If a child leaves its initiative while a reader or action menu is open, return to a nearby child or the empty parent before another action. Removing an unrelated initiative does not change the active ticket queue. Removing an inactive remembered child also leaves unrelated queue and home initiative action menus open on their canonical targets.
Press 5 for Ready, 6 for Review, 7 for Blocked, or 8 for All to open the separate ticket queues. Press h to return to initiatives.
Queue headings and active controls identify the selected queue. Queues contain tickets only; initiative navigation keeps its own selection and scroll position.
Queue rows separate type, stable ID, title, and canonical ticket state. Next shows the eligible action; Recorded shows the phase and status from a validated workflow receipt. Review readiness does not mean a review is running.
Press Enter on a queue ticket to open its canonical detail in its initiative or Ungrouped context. Return navigation restores the queue selection and scroll position.
In an empty filtered queue, press 8 to open All or h to return to initiatives. Empty queues offer no ticket actions. Available actions identify their canonical target and explain disabled reasons.
Uppercase R refreshes. Lowercase r retains its existing Review action. The a action menu and direct action keys keep their existing safety checks.
Loading, empty collections, unreadable records, and refresh failures have distinct messages. A failed refresh retains readable content and blocks unsafe transitions.
`/shared-context files` opens the independent Files workspace. Files keeps its path-insertion behavior.

Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move between tracker panes, workspace tabs, and the Projects breadcrumb.
Press Enter on Projects, or click Projects, to open the project list.
Type to filter project names and identities. Matching ignores case and accepts substrings or characters in order. Projects shows the filtered/total count and active query. Use Backspace to edit or Ctrl+U to clear. A zero-result list cannot open a project. Use the arrow keys to select a result. Press Enter to open it. Printable keys, including q, 1 and 2, enter search text while the Projects list has focus.
The list includes stored shared-context projects and the current project. Stable identities distinguish equal names and remove duplicate projects.

The header displays Shared or Repo from the selected alignment route. The indicator does not change storage.
Project selection changes only the modal. It does not change the Pi session directory or system instructions.
Each project keeps its tracker navigation, selection, scroll position, and independent Files state.
Project changes stop the old watchers. Return navigation resolves routes before it starts the selected project's watchers and reads.

Outside Projects, press 1 for Tracker or 2 for Files. At the tracker root, Esc opens Projects. At Projects, Esc closes the modal even with an active filter.
Files keeps its existing escape and path-insertion behavior.

Stored projects do not contain checkout locations. Shared initialization and route migration save the credential-free canonical remote in `.context-project.json`. Stored project resolution uses this identity for hosted trackers; it never treats the directory slug as a remote. Older stores without this file can still read local records. Hosted trackers need explicit identity recovery. Run `scripts/shared-context/cli.ts list`, then use exactly one authoritative source:

```text
scripts/shared-context/cli.ts recover-identity SLUG --checkout /verified/checkout
scripts/shared-context/cli.ts recover-identity SLUG --remote https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git
```

The checkout command reads that checkout’s Git origin. The remote command works without a checkout. Both require an existing store whose slug matches the supplied origin. Recovery writes only missing credential-free identity metadata. It preserves existing metadata, routes, records, and session instructions. Reopen Projects after recovery. If neither the authoritative remote nor a verified checkout is available, hosted tickets remain unavailable; the directory slug cannot recover that identity. No repository scan, initialization, migration, or clone runs.
If the current checkout disappears while the modal is open, its existing shared directory remains reachable through the deduplicated current entry. Returning to a cached workspace refreshes checkout capability, disabled actions, Files roots, and watcher targets before it reads records. Selected-project reads use a verified surviving directory from that project, even if the original repository-only session checkout disappears. The Pi session directory stays unchanged.
For mixed routes, repository-backed records remain unavailable until a checkout is known.
Files can still browse the stored shared directory. Checkout-dependent actions display a disabled reason.
Open the command from that project's checkout to use those actions. The modal does not search other repositories or create a project registry.

Fresh-chat actions use Pi's replacement session context to stage the command. The command stays unsent until you press Enter.

limitations: Actual offline Pi production extension and MQ records, real validated implementation receipt and registered worktree skill; no AI inference or workflow dispatch.
